newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends up sharply on exports, soyoil up.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends up sharply on exports, soyoil up.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures ended sharply higher and a contract high was notched in the July on surprisingly high USDA weekly export sales data, traders said.
Soyoil was also higher in line with gains in soybeans.
"They're exporting beans at the expense of meal in Brazil, so people are still coming to the U.S. for meal," said one veteran trader.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture reported weekly soymeal export sales of 209,800 tonnes. That figure was higher than trade expectations for 80,000 to 150,000 tonnes.
Soyoil sales were a lackluster 6,500 tonnes.

"Demand has been good enough that the U.S. markets have been very competitive with the South American markets, which is incredibly unusual for this time of year," said Jack Scoville, analyst at LIT America.

Scoville and others said they had expected U.S. exports to drop sharply as Brazil began shipping soybeans and soymeal. But a variety of problems ranging from mechanical difficulties to strikes have hampered Brazil's export pace.
Soymeal closed $6.00 to $1.50 per ton higher with May up $6.00 at $282.70. Soyoil ended 0.29 to 0.17 cent per lb higher with May up 0.17 at 24.42.
The new contract high for the July is $281.50 per ton, topping the previous high of $279.80 set on March 20.
Commercials were aggressive buyers of soymeal and soyoil on the day. Cargill Inc bought a total of 1,200 lots soymeal and at least 700 lots soyoil on the day.
Central Soya and Continental Grain were also noted buyers of soymeal while ADM, Produce Grain and Term Commodities were buyers of soyoil.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 16,000 lots, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 13,271 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 12,000 lots, against Wednesday's 9,497 lots.
